newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Black sells out stake in Australia's Fairfax group.
newsitem.headline: Black sells out stake in Australia's Fairfax group.

text.p: Canadian media mogul Conrad Black is to sell off his 25 percent stake in Australia's Fairfax group to New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd, Brierley said on Monday.

Under a deal approved by the Australian government, Brierley said it would initially buy 20 percent of John Fairfax Holdings Ltd for A$447.1 million ($353.2 million) from Black's Hollinger International Inc.
It had a conditional agreement to purchase the remaining five percent stake held for another A$106.7 million, subject to Fairfax shareholders approval.
Brierley is an investment group based in Auckland, New Zealand, which is noted for taking strategic stakes in companies and then selling at a profit.

The Fairfax group, Australia's oldest media group and publisher of major titles such as the Sydney Morning Herald and The Melbourne Age, went bankrupt in 1991. It was rescued under a deal engineered by Black which saw 80 percent of it floated and left him with a 15 percent stake, later raised to 25 percent.
Black's stake was held through The Telegraph Plc, a unit of Hollinger which publishes the London Daily Telegraph.
Fairfax has been subject of much ownership speculation with Black, News Corp's Rupert Murdoch and Australian billionaire Kerry Packer all variously building up stakes in recent years.
But the situation has been muddied by government rules, currently under review, on foreign and cross-media ownership.
News Corp sold off its stake, which was just below five percent, last month. Packer still owns 15 percent of Fairfax but is not allowed to increase that because of his television holdings.
